findings.where: First screen (hero) at both widths, the navigation, and the foot of the page
findings.fault: There is no way to reach Mark anywhere on the page. The hero has no action, the email address appears nowhere, the nav has no Contact item and the footer has no address. The parts map lists no mailto link or contact link at all. The palette and texture notes describe a pad-yellow 'address strip' at the foot of the sheet, but the page never renders it.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has decided Mark fits their terms of reference and finds no address to write to. The founder too: the brief requires one action with Mark.Moseley@MMMinfra.com shown on the first screen, and the personal-advisor test asks for one direct, personal way to reach him.

findings.where: Motion sketch panel (desktop-05; phone-03 and phone-04)
findings.fault: The motion specimen sits on a large lilac field. Lilac is not one of the tile's four colours, and it is the one large coloured area on the page. On it, the blue curve and the blue 'Replay the entrance' link sit on a hue the palette never names. This contradicts the brief's single soft ground with only blue and grey as ink, and the tile's own note that purple backdrops are turned to ink.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges whether the direction keeps to the house blue and grey on one quiet ground. A lilac block reads as a stray colour, not as Counsel's paper.

findings.where: Article specimen: the subheads 'So, what are the key ‘chapter topics’?' and 'Download'
findings.fault: The subheads are set in a heavy, wide black grotesque. That is a third face, used nowhere else. It contradicts the type-pair card, which gives subheads to Newsreader 500, and it shouts against the light serif and quiet Public Sans around it.
findings.who_objects: A reader of Mark's article, who gets a loud, poster-like break in a page meant to read like a legal journal. The founder, who asked for refined and serious type, and Angélique, who needs one clear subhead style to reuse.

findings.where: Article specimen: the 'Download' link's metadata running into the motion panel (desktop-04 bottom, phone-03)
findings.fault: The lilac motion panel starts directly under the download item with no space between them. On the phone, the line 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF' touches the panel's top edge, so the end of the article looks as if it belongs to the next block.
findings.who_objects: Anyone reading the specimen as a page. The article's last item, the PDF the research calls 'the product', loses its own space and reads as cut off.

findings.fault: Four like parts are drawn four ways: a square-cornered box with a hairline border, a rounded rectangle, an ellipse, and a square box with a thick blue border. The shapes suggest differences of meaning the colours don't have. The blue edge on the yellow swatch looks like a selected state.
findings.who_objects: The founder, comparing palettes across tiles, who has to work out whether the shape means something. It also clashes with the tile's own rule of one square-cornered hairline frame.

findings.fault: The texture swatch is an empty framed box with a yellow bar filling part of its bottom edge. It reads as a half-filled progress bar, not as a sheet of paper with a strip of yellow at its foot.
findings.who_objects: The founder, trying to picture how the legal-pad colour will appear. The swatch shows a UI loading bar instead.

findings.fault: A button (parts map: button) is styled as an underlined blue prose link. It borrows the link's signifier for an action that stays on the page.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who expects an underlined blue phrase to take them somewhere. The house's reserved-property rule also keeps the underline for navigation.
